article_title: Breaking Bad Behaviors: A New Tool for Learning Classroom Management Using Virtual Reality
citation: Lugrin J-L, Latoschik ME, Habel M, Roth D, Seufert C and Grafe S (2016) Breaking Bad Behaviors: A New Tool for Learning Classroom Management Using Virtual Reality. Front. ICT 3:26. https://doi.org/10.3389/fict.2016.00026
title: 3B (Breaking Bad Behaviors): an immersive VR classroom management training system with teacher HMD immersion and instructor desktop control console
description: 3B is a collaborative VR platform in which a trainee teacher is immersed in a real-time 3D virtual classroom of twenty-four semi-autonomous virtual students via a head-mounted display and headphones, while an instructor controls training tasks and feedback through a 2D graphical desktop console. The system uses a client-server architecture on Unreal Engine 4 with Oculus Rift DK2 and Kinect v2 markerless tracking, and was designed as a companion tool for CRM seminars at the University of Würzburg so lecturers can "link theory with practice using the medium of VR". It is built from low-cost consumer hardware and free software for use by practitioners without technical expertise.
requirements: Usable by practitioners without expert knowledge in computer programming or virtual reality; instructors must be able to create new training scenarios without deep technical knowledge
constraints: The physical self is not artificially augmented with sensors; the teacher wears minimum equipment and the system does not impede natural body movement
target_learners: Trainee primary and secondary school teachers in initial teacher education
target_learning_goals: Classroom management skills, particularly preempting, controlling, and mitigating disruptive student behavior
examples: Used in two seminars at the University of Würzburg: Classroom Management and Videobased Reflection of Education
